about: As he ascends the altar steps, the priest asks God to take away iniquity so that we may enter the “Sancta sanctórum”, the holy of holies. In the second prayer he asks, in his own name, that his sins be forgiven through the merits of the saints whose relics are in this place, and of all the saints, kissing the altar as he names them.

seg.nr: The priest extends and joins his hands, then says one word aloud.
The priest ascends the steps to the altar and continues silently.

seg.tr: Lord, we ask You to take away our iniquities, so that with pure minds we may be worthy to enter the Holy of Holies.

fn.w002: Imperative of aufero, a compound of ab and fero.
fn.w005: Parenthetic polite formula inserted between the verb and its object.
fn.w009: Introduces a purpose clause with “mereámur” (w014) in the subjunctive.
fn.w011: An adjective used as a noun in the neuter plural: holy things. With “sanctórum” (w012) it forms “the Holy of Holies”.
fn.w012: Neuter genitive plural dependent on the substantivized “Sancta” (w011), forming the expression Holy of Holies.

seg.nr: With joined hands resting on the altar the priest bows over it and begins the second prayer.

seg.tr: We ask You, Lord, by the merits of Your saints,

fn.w022: Present indicative, first person plural. Compare the subjunctive “Orémus” (w001).
fn.w027: Substantivized adjective, genitive plural: of the Saints.

seg.nr: The priest kisses the middle of the altar.

seg.tr: whose relics are here, and by the merits of all the saints, that You may be pleased to forgive all my sins. Amen.

fn.w029: Genitive plural relative pronoun referring to “Sanctórum” (w027).
fn.w030: Nominative subject of the relative clause.
fn.w036: Introduces a purpose clause with “dignéris” (w038) in the subjunctive.
fn.w041: Possessive adjective, accusative neuter plural, agreeing with “peccáta” (w040). The possessor is singular.
